get.description:
Liveness + capabilities + cascade readiness probe.

``status`` stays ``"ok"`` whenever the process is up — the HTTP code
is a *liveness* signal and a degraded cascade must not trigger a
restart (a crash-loop fixes neither a bad md file nor disk bloat).
The ``cascade`` block is the *readiness* signal: ``healthy=false``
with human-readable ``reasons`` **only** when the projection pipeline
itself is stuck (drain failing, optimize stuck, version cleanup
stalled). ``failed_permanent`` — files awaiting ``cascade fix`` — is
a data-quality backlog reported as an informational count that does
not flip ``healthy``. Alert on ``cascade.healthy``.

The ``decider`` block names the multi-round decider and says whether it
answered the startup probe, and how many rounds failed since.
Render the current Prometheus registry in exposition format.

post.description:
Add messages into the conversation pipeline (chat memory).

With ``group_id`` the session becomes (or already is) a group session:
its messages become group memory, never per-sender personal memory.
Without it, a session of three or more people (role ``user`` senders) is
their implicit group; one or two people's conversation is their own
memory, each person keeping a copy of every segment.
``rejected`` / ``failed`` count the non-text items dropped at ingest; a
queued batch (202) is ingested later and logs them
(``memorize.ingest_dropped``). A group takes each message once:
``duplicates`` counts the messages it already held, which were skipped
(a queued batch logs them, ``memorize.duplicates_skipped``).

schema.title: Response Add Memory Api V1 Memory Add Post

202.description: Queued: async_mode, or the session already had a backlog

403.description: Roster events from an asker who may not send them, or a batch to a group with a deliverer from anyone else

409.description: Session bound to another group, or a roster conflict

429.description: Queue at its per-session or global cap

post.description:
Force boundary detection over the current ``session_id`` buffer.

Runs inline unless the session still has queued batches, in which case
the flush joins the queue behind them and answers 202. A session of a
group with a deliverer is flushed by its deliverer only.

post.description:
Multi-round retrieval over a user's or a group's memory.

``method`` other than ``llm_multiround`` and an ``agent_id`` (EverOS 2.0 has
no agent memory) are refused (422). A group scope (``group_id`` /
``group_ids``) needs an ``asker_id`` who is a current member; it returns
only what lies inside the asker's membership windows (403 for a
non-member).
Paginated listing over the requested ``memory_type``, in the read scope.

Forget one user's memories, one session's, or one user's of a session.

EverOS 2.0 has no hard delete: this is ``POST /memory/forget`` with an
``owner`` or ``session`` target, run at once. Nothing leaves markdown; the
answer's ``forget_ids`` (one per user reached) undo it. With ``group_id``
it is the group's delete (docs/group-memory.md, section 15): an owner's or
admin's forget of one session or one member's messages -- soft and
propagated -- whose ``forget_id`` undoes it.

403.description: Group-scoped: the asker is not an owner or admin

422.description: No scope, an agent_id (2.0 has no agent memory), or a session bound to a group without group_id

500.description: Forget incomplete; send the same request again

503.description: SESSION_BUSY: the session is still being memorized; nothing was forgotten, retry later

post.description:
Forget episodes by id (EverOS 2.0 has no hard delete).

``POST /memory/forget`` with a ``record`` target, per owner, run at once;
the answer's ``forget_ids`` undo it. Ids that match nothing are skipped
(not 404); sending the same request again forgets nothing more.

500.description: Forget incomplete; send the same request again

post.description:
Forget in a user's memory or a group's, reversibly; a dry run by default.

A body naming ``user_id`` and a ``target`` forgets in the user's memory:
records by id (``record``), one conversation (``session``), everything
(``owner``), the memories of some kinds in a time range (``condition``),
or a picture (``image``). A body naming ``group_id`` forgets inside the
group (docs/group-memory.md, section 5.5). Both are a **dry run** unless
``dry_run`` is false: the answer then says what the forget would touch.
A real forget answers with what it touched and its ``forget_id``, which
``/forget/undo`` takes. The picture body (``user_id`` + ``image_id``) is
the picture forget, run at once.

403.description: Someone else's personal memory; a group asker who is not a current member, or not allowed this target

404.description: A user's record id that names nothing; or the group holds no such message, session, member, record or picture

500.description: Forget incomplete; send the same request again

503.description: A conversation the forget touches is busy; nothing was forgotten, retry later

post.description:
Forget one conversation's memories for one user, at once and reversibly.

An alias of ``/forget`` with a ``session`` target and ``dry_run: false``:
the conversation's current episode versions and picture memories are
marked, and ``/forget/session/undo`` (or ``/forget/undo`` with the
``forget_id``) reverses it. A picture file survives while any other live
memory still references it. A profile item goes once every segment it
rests on is forgotten.

500.description: Forget incomplete; send the same request again

503.description: The conversation is being memorized; nothing was forgotten, retry later

post.description: Undo the newest forget of one conversation for one user.

Write a revised version of one picture memory; the old one is superseded.

An alias of ``/memory/update`` for a picture memory, by its hash. The
picture is the same picture: only what the memory says changes. The new
entry supersedes the old, and the cascade recomputes its keyword index
and vector from the new text.

409.description: The named occurrence was replaced (VERSION_CONFLICT) or forgotten (MEMORY_FORGOTTEN)

post.description:
Undo a forget: a user's by ``forget_id``, a group's, or a picture's newest.

A body naming ``user_id`` and ``forget_id`` undoes that forget of the user
(any target): exactly what it marked comes back, except what another
live forget names too. A body naming ``group_id`` undoes the group forget
``forget_id``, with the forget's own authorisation; 409 when a later
forget rewrote what it wrote (undo that one first). The picture body
(``user_id`` + ``image_id``) undoes the picture's newest forget.
``applied: false`` means there was nothing to undo (already undone, or
never forgotten).

403.description: Someone else's personal memory; a group asker not allowed the forget it reverses

409.description: Group undo: a later forget rewrote what this one wrote; undo that one first

500.description: Undo incomplete; send the same request again

get.description:
One stored picture, by id, as bytes.

``model`` renders at ``[images] model_edge`` and ``cache_quality`` -- the
copy extraction read the picture at and the one to show an answering model.
``thumbnail`` renders at ``[decider].image_thumbnail_edge`` — the same size
the retrieval loop shows the decider — so a caller can preview exactly what
it saw. A copy is JPEG, or PNG for a greyscale picture, and is labelled as
what it is. A picture the asker may not see answers exactly as one that does
not exist (docs/group-memory.md, section 9.1).

for index convergence (two consecutive zero samples to guard against the

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Unfinished queued batches of this session, this one included

AcceptedResponseData.title: AcceptedResponseData
AcceptedResponseData.description: 202 body: the batch is persisted and queued for the memorize worker.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: Pictures refused at ingest: over a [images] limit (bytes, per message, per request), not a picture, or unreadable. The rest of their message is kept.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Non-text items that could not be read into text (a parser call that failed). The rest of their message is kept.

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.description: Messages of the batch its group already held, skipped: by message_id when one was sent, else by sender, timestamp and content. Present only when the batch had some.

AudienceItem.title: AudienceItem
AudienceItem.description:
Who knew a group record (docs/group-memory.md, section 8.6).

Computed at read time from the roster and the record's sources; shown only
on records the asker can see.

index_rows.title: Index Rows
index_rows.description: Rows per business index table, counted once when the process started. A snapshot, not a live count: counting costs a round trip per collection on a remote backend and this endpoint is polled. `everos cascade status` counts live.

index_emptied.title: Index Emptied
index_emptied.description: True when the cascade ledger says every file is indexed, nothing is pending, and every index table is empty -- the state left behind by deleting the index directory, which the ledger in .index/sqlite survives. Searches return nothing while every other signal here reads healthy. Recover with `everos cascade rebuild`; markdown is untouched. Informational like failed_permanent: it does not flip `healthy`, because it is a startup snapshot that could not clear until a restart.

unreadable_entries.title: Unreadable Entries
unreadable_entries.description: Entries of indexed markdown files that the projection skipped because they no longer parse (a hand edit broke them); the rest of each file is indexed. Each is logged as `markdown_entry_unreadable`, and `everos cascade status` names the files. Informational like failed_permanent: it does not flip `healthy`.

CascadeHealthBlock.title: CascadeHealthBlock
CascadeHealthBlock.description:
Readiness of the md → LanceDB projection (cascade) subsystem.

``healthy`` reflects **operational** health only — drain loop alive,
optimize not stuck, version cleanup (prune) not stalled — and is what
alerting should watch. ``failed_permanent`` (md files awaiting
``cascade fix``) is a normal data-quality backlog reported as an
informational count; it does **not** flip ``healthy``, otherwise the
signal would sit red forever.

ConstraintItem.title: ConstraintItem
ConstraintItem.description:
One thing an answer must respect (docs/group-memory.md, section 8.4).

Built after the search loop from the core: a group-profile item linked to
it (a decision, a dissent, a topic's status) whose quote and speakers were
verified when it was written, or -- for a core record no item covers -- a
metadata constraint quoting the record's best-matching source message.
Every quote is a verbatim part of the message it cites.

ConstraintScopeItem.title: ConstraintScopeItem
ConstraintScopeItem.description: Where a constraint applies: the group, or some of its members.

ConstraintSourceItem.title: ConstraintSourceItem
ConstraintSourceItem.description: The message a constraint quotes: verbatim, from its segment.

ContentItemDTO.title: ContentItemDTO
ContentItemDTO.description: Content piece (v1 API brief appendix A).

base_url.title: Base Url
base_url.description: Its endpoint (scheme, host, port and path only).

reachable.title: Reachable
reachable.description: Whether it answered the startup probe; null while the probe runs or when the client cannot be probed.

probe_error.title: Probe Error
probe_error.description: Why the probe failed, when it did.

rounds.title: Rounds
rounds.description: Rounds asked of it since the server started.

failed_rounds.title: Failed Rounds
failed_rounds.description: Of those, the rounds that fell back or were salvaged.

DeciderHealthBlock.title: DeciderHealthBlock
DeciderHealthBlock.description:
The multi-round decider: what it is, its startup probe, its rounds since.

``reachable`` is the startup probe's verdict and never changes afterwards
(a polled endpoint must not call a model). ``failed_rounds`` and
``last_failure`` come from the searches themselves, so a decider that
stopped answering after startup shows there. A failed round still answers
the search (``data.degraded`` names it); it is not an outage of search.

DeleteByIdsRequest.title: DeleteByIdsRequest
DeleteByIdsRequest.description:
Episodes to delete, by memory id ``<owner_id>_<entry_id>``.

A forget of those episodes (target ``record``, per owner): nothing leaves
markdown. The whole request is rejected (422, nothing forgotten) if any id
is not an episode id of a path-safe owner with a real date.

DeleteByIdsResponseData.title: DeleteByIdsResponseData
DeleteByIdsResponseData.description:
``{"memory_type": "episode", "success": true}`` (Cloud's shape), with
the forgets it ran (``forget_ids``, one per owner).

DeleteReason.title: DeleteReason
DeleteReason.description: Why the caller deletes: logged as ``code``; ``note`` is never logged.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: A group-scoped delete: an owner's or admin's forget of one session (session_id) or one member's messages (user_id).

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who asks, for a group-scoped delete (an owner or admin).

DeleteRequest.title: DeleteRequest
DeleteRequest.description:
Which memories to delete: an owner, a session, or one owner's session.

At least one of ``user_id`` and ``session_id``. EverOS 2.0 has no hard
delete: a delete is a forget of the same scope (``POST /memory/forget``,
run at once), reversible by the ``forget_ids`` it answers with. EverOS 2.0
has no agent memory: an ``agent_id`` is refused (422).

With ``group_id`` the delete is the group's (docs/group-memory.md,
section 15): an owner's or admin's forget -- soft, propagated, undone by
the returned ``forget_id`` -- of one of the group's sessions
(``session_id``) or of one member's messages (``user_id``, the member).
``asker_id`` names the owner or admin.

DeleteResponseData.title: DeleteResponseData
DeleteResponseData.description:
What a delete forgot: EverOS 2.0 has no hard delete.

Attributes:
    filters: The scope fields the request set.
    count: Memories taken out of default reads (episodes, picture
        memories, scenes and profile items marked forgotten).
    forget_ids: The forgets it ran, one per user it reached;
        ``POST /memory/forget/undo`` takes each.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error codes returned in the API error envelope.

Each code maps to exactly one HTTP status code. Clients can switch on
this value to decide retry / display / routing behaviour without parsing
the human-readable ``message`` field.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: Inner ``error`` object in the canonical error envelope.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Canonical error envelope returned by all error handlers.

FilterNode.title: FilterNode
FilterNode.description:
One Filters DSL node.

Recursive ``AND`` / ``OR`` arrays mix with arbitrary scalar fields at
the same level. Pydantic only checks the combinators; field-level
safety is enforced when compiling the node to a LanceDB ``where``
string in :mod:`everos.memory.search.filters`.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Not taken here: a body that names a group is a group forget (group_id, asker_id, target).

ForgetImageRequest.title: ForgetImageRequest
ForgetImageRequest.description:
Which picture to forget, for which user.

A picture is owned per user even though its file is shared: the memories
written about it are the user's, and one user forgetting a picture must not
take it out of another user's memory.

ForgetImageResponseData.title: ForgetImageResponseData
ForgetImageResponseData.description:
What a forget touched.

``episodes`` are the entry ids of the *new* versions written without the
picture. The versions they supersede are still in markdown, on purpose:
asking what was said before a forget has to keep working.

``pictures`` lists the picture memories themselves, in entry order;
``image_memories`` repeats its length so a caller that only needs the
count does not have to walk it.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Refused (422): a conversation of a group is forgotten with POST /memory/forget and a session target.

ForgetSessionRequest.title: ForgetSessionRequest
ForgetSessionRequest.description:
Which conversation to forget, for which user.

Reversible, unlike ``POST /memory/delete``: a delete removes memories, a
forget marks them and can be undone. The session's picture files survive
while any other live memory references them.

ForgetSessionResponseData.title: ForgetSessionResponseData
ForgetSessionResponseData.description:
What forgetting one conversation touched.

``episodes`` are entry ids marked forgotten, ``image_memories`` how many
picture memories, ``images`` the picture *files* taken out of
circulation because this session held their last live reference, and
``profiles`` how many profile items left ``user.md`` because every segment
they rest on is now forgotten.

ForgottenMessageData.title: ForgottenMessageData
ForgottenMessageData.description: One message a group forget marked forgotten.

ForgottenPictureData.title: ForgottenPictureData
ForgottenPictureData.description:
One picture memory the request touched.

``entry_id`` names the occurrence, ``image_id`` the file, and ``name`` is
what the client called the picture on that arrival — provenance a caller
needs to map the memory back to its own input.

GetData.title: GetData
GetData.description:
Body of ``response.data``.

Every array is always present so client code can iterate without
branching on ``memory_type``; the route populates exactly one.

GetImageItem.title: GetImageItem
GetImageItem.description: A group picture memory listing item -- one appearance of one picture.

GetMemoryType.title: GetMemoryType
GetMemoryType.description:
The kinds enumerated by ``/get``.

``episode``, ``profile`` and ``scene`` are user-owned; the group kinds
need a group scope. Cross-pairs are rejected by
:meth:`GetRequest._validate_owner_memory_type_pair`.

GetProfileItem.title: GetProfileItem
GetProfileItem.description:
A user's profile, or a member's profile inside a group.

A member-in-group profile (``owner_type = group``) holds only the items
the asker's windows allow.

GetRequest.title: GetRequest
GetRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v2/memory/get``.

Callers identify the memory owner via ``user_id`` or a group scope --
exactly one must be set. Internally the manager keeps using
``owner_id`` / ``owner_type`` (the storage tables' columns); those
are exposed as derived properties so the rename only affects the
wire contract. An ``agent_id`` is refused with :data:`NO_AGENT_MEMORY`.

roster.title: Roster
roster.description: Current members; every interval with include_history=true.

deliverer_id.title: Deliverer Id
deliverer_id.description: The group's deliverer, or null when anyone may deliver.

GroupDeleteResponseData.title: GroupDeleteResponseData
GroupDeleteResponseData.description:
What a group-scoped delete forgot, and the forget's id for its undo.

Attributes:
    filters: The scope fields the request set.
    count: Records taken out of the group's memory.
    forget_id: The forget it ran (``POST /memory/forget/undo`` takes it).

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who asks; required unless the identity header names them.

GroupForgetRequest.title: GroupForgetRequest
GroupForgetRequest.description:
A forget inside a group (docs/group-memory.md, section 5.5).

Who may forget what: a message its sender, a member that member, a record
a member whose own messages alone it rests on, a picture its poster; the
group's owners and admins anything; a session only they. A former member
or a stranger is refused (403). ``dry_run`` (default **true**) changes
nothing and answers with exactly what the real run would touch; send
``dry_run: false`` to forget.

GroupForgetResponseData.title: GroupForgetResponseData
GroupForgetResponseData.description:
What a forget inside a group touched (or would, on a dry run).

Records are named as the read side names them (``<group>_<entry>``);
member-profile items by their ``item_id``. ``episodes`` are the versions
taken out -- each either rewritten (``rewritten`` new versions, ids in
``new_episodes``) or dropped when nothing of its segment was left.
``stale_*`` items were taken out and are written again from their
remaining sources by the profile's next update.

GroupProfileEntry.title: GroupProfileEntry
GroupProfileEntry.description:
One group-profile item (docs/group-memory.md, section 7.5).

``kind`` decides which fields are filled: a topic its ``topic_id`` /
``name`` / ``summary`` / ``topic_status``; a decision its ``statement``
and the people fields; a dissent ``statement`` / ``held_by`` / ``about``;
a role ``member_id`` / ``role`` / ``confidence``. ``status`` is the
item's own (``current``, ``open``, ``active``, a topic's status ...) or
``superseded`` once a later item replaced it.

GroupUndoForgetRequest.title: GroupUndoForgetRequest
GroupUndoForgetRequest.description: Undo one forget of a group by its id, with the forget's own authorisation.

GroupUndoForgetResponseData.title: GroupUndoForgetResponseData
GroupUndoForgetResponseData.description:
What an undo of a group forget put back.

``applied`` is ``False`` when the forget was undone already. ``withdrawn``
are the records the forget had written, now taken out again.

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who asks. Required unless the deployment's identity header ([access] identity_header) carries it; a different value there is 403.

deliverer_id.title: Deliverer Id
deliverer_id.description: The identity the gateway asserts for the group's key: the one program that forwards the group's chat. Once set, only it may add messages to the group's sessions or flush them, and it holds every right of an owner. Left out: unchanged; null: cleared. Set and cleared by owners, admins and the deliverer itself.

GroupUpsertRequest.title: GroupUpsertRequest
GroupUpsertRequest.description: ``PUT /groups/{group_id}``: create the group, or update its meta.

embed.title: Embed
embed.description: Whether the embedding service answered the startup dimension probe. A snapshot taken when the process started, not a liveness check: a service that recovers later still reads false until the next restart.

decider.title: Decider
decider.description: Whether the multi-round decider answered the startup probe (one request with max_tokens=1, sent in the background when the server starts). A snapshot like `embed`: false while the probe runs; see the `decider` block for why it failed and for the rounds since.

HealthCapabilities.title: HealthCapabilities
HealthCapabilities.description:
Availability flags for the capability probes.

Field order matches the health-endpoint payload contract; clients
key off these names to decide whether to expose optional features.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Response schema for ``GET /health``.

Declared as a Pydantic model (not ``dict``) so the generated
OpenAPI schema carries the full field shape — ``capabilities``,
``disabled_features`` and ``cascade`` are typed. A bare ``-> dict``
return type degrades the OpenAPI response to
``additionalProperties: true``, which robs clients (and codegen) of
any structure to lean on.

ImageTarget.title: ImageTarget
ImageTarget.description: The group's memories of one picture, by content hash.

MemberIntervalDTO.title: MemberIntervalDTO
MemberIntervalDTO.description: One membership interval, ``[joined_at, left_at)`` in epoch ms.

MemberTarget.title: MemberTarget
MemberTarget.description: Every message one member sent in the group, and their profile in it.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The group the session belongs to. The first batch naming it binds the session; a later batch without it inherits the binding; a batch naming another group is 409. An unknown group is created ([groups] implicit_create).

roster.title: Roster
roster.description: Roster events applied before the messages (an event without `at` takes the batch's first message time). For an existing group the asker must be an owner or admin.

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who sends the batch; needed for roster events of an existing group, and for any batch to a group with a deliverer, which takes batches from its deliverer only (403 otherwise). The gateway's identity header, when configured, is the asker instead.

defer_extraction.title: Defer Extraction
defer_extraction.description: Persist messages in the durable unprocessed buffer without running boundary detection or extraction. A later /flush commits the batch.

async_mode.title: Async Mode
async_mode.description: Persist the batch to the memorize queue and return 202 at once instead of running boundary detection and extraction inline. Poll GET /tasks/{request_id}. A session that already has queued batches is queued even when this is false, so batches never run out of order.

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who flushes; read only for a session of a group with a deliverer, which only its deliverer may flush (403 otherwise). The gateway's identity header, when configured, is the asker instead.

MemorizeQueueHealthBlock.title: MemorizeQueueHealthBlock
MemorizeQueueHealthBlock.description:
Readiness of the ``async_mode`` memorize queue.

``healthy`` is the delivery loop being alive. The probe only observes;
the loop relaunches itself (and on the next ``/add``), and
``loop_restarts`` counts how often that happened. ``pending`` and
``oldest_pending_age_s`` are the backlog: growing with a live loop means
delivery is slower than arrival (or the LLM is down), which is a
capacity signal, not a liveness one. Alert on ``healthy`` and on
``loop_restarts`` changing.

MemoryHistoryResponseData.title: MemoryHistoryResponseData
MemoryHistoryResponseData.description: Every version of one memory the asker may see, current first.

MemoryVersionData.title: MemoryVersionData
MemoryVersionData.description:
One version of a memory.

``state`` is ``current``, ``superseded`` (a newer version replaced it),
``merged`` (a merge of several did) or ``forgotten``; ``next`` the version
that replaced it. ``sources`` say what it rests on (times there in epoch
ms), ``content`` what it says.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Message event time as Unix epoch in **milliseconds** (v1 API contract; the algo layer auto-detects sec vs ms for backward compat but the contract is ms).

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Optional client id of the message: the chat platform's id, unique within the group. Kept for a group session (message-level forget, source quotes) and what the group dedupes by -- a message whose id the group already holds, in any of its sessions, is skipped; ignored on a one-to-one session.

MessageTarget.title: MessageTarget
MessageTarget.description: Messages of one session of the group, by id.

ProfileSourceItem.title: ProfileSourceItem
ProfileSourceItem.description: One verified piece of evidence: a message of a segment, quoted verbatim.

ProjectDTO.title: ProjectDTO
ProjectDTO.description: ``GET /projects/{project_id}``: the asker's groups and their members.

ProjectGroupDTO.title: ProjectGroupDTO
ProjectGroupDTO.description: One group of the project the asker is in.

ProjectMemberDTO.title: ProjectMemberDTO
ProjectMemberDTO.description: A current member of the asker's groups, with the groups they share.

ProjectProfileDTO.title: ProjectProfileDTO
ProjectProfileDTO.description:
``GET /projects/{project_id}/profile``: the visible current items.

Each item names its group (``group_id``); oldest first. The same decision
taken in two groups is two items.

QuestionPicture.title: QuestionPicture
QuestionPicture.description:
A picture attached to the question itself, not to the memory.

Same content-item shape as ``/memory/add`` (``uri`` or ``base64``, plus
``ext`` and an optional ``name``), because a caller that can send a picture
to one endpoint should not have to learn a second shape for the other.

A question picture is **content-addressed in ``figures/`` and establishes
nothing**: no picture memory, no reference count, no profile item. It exists
for one search — the decider looks at it every round — and "what I asked
with" is not a fact about the user. Storing it by hash is what lets the
decider read it from the same place it reads a candidate, and lets the same
question asked twice pay for the file once.

QuiesceResponse.title: QuiesceResponse
QuiesceResponse.description:
What the final drain accomplished, and what it left behind.

``pending_before`` is the queue depth on arrival: a caller that expected the
projection to be up to date can assert it was 0 and learn otherwise. Anything
above 0 in ``pending_after`` means the drain could not finish -- the index is
NOT a complete projection of the markdown, and searching it will silently
under-recall.

RecordTarget.title: RecordTarget
RecordTarget.description: Records by id: episodes, picture memories, scenes, profile items.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Not taken here: a body that names a group is a group forget (group_id, asker_id, target).

ReviseImageMemoryRequest.title: ReviseImageMemoryRequest
ReviseImageMemoryRequest.description:
Change one picture memory's description and/or in-picture text.

Same scope fields and picture id as a forget; ``entry_id`` selects which
occurrence when the picture has several (otherwise the current one). Both
text fields are optional but at least one is required - a request that
changes nothing is a caller bug, not a no-op.

Deliberately not a ``PATCH`` of arbitrary fields: the picture's identity,
path and time belong to the arrival, and "edit" here means what the memory
*says*, not what it *is*.

ReviseImageMemoryResponseData.title: ReviseImageMemoryResponseData
ReviseImageMemoryResponseData.description: The version that was written, and the one it replaced.

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who asks. Required unless the deployment's identity header ([access] identity_header) carries it; a different value there is 403.

at.title: At
at.description: Epoch ms the event takes effect; defaults to now.

RosterEventDTO.title: RosterEventDTO
RosterEventDTO.description:
One roster event: ``join`` opens an interval, ``leave`` closes it,
``update`` changes ``display_name`` / ``aliases`` / ``role`` / ``title``.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description: One strategy run within a trigger response.

SearchData.title: SearchData
SearchData.description:
Body of ``response.data``.

All arrays are always present so client code can iterate without
branching on ``owner_type``. Routes not applicable to the request's
owner type stay as ``[]``. ``unprocessed_messages`` is filled only
when ``filters.session_id`` is present as a top-level eq scalar —
in-flight buffer rows are scope-tagged but unattributed (no
``user_id``), so session is the only meaningful query dimension.

SearchDegradation.title: SearchDegradation
SearchDegradation.description:
A part of this search that did not run as configured.

Today one kind: a multi-round round the decider did not decide. Its
candidates were still ranked, but which of them are core was not the
decider's choice, and the loop stopped there.

SearchEpisodeItem.title: SearchEpisodeItem
SearchEpisodeItem.description:
Episode hit — always user-scoped in the current emission contract.

``type`` is narrowed to ``"Conversation"`` because the only emitted
episode shape today is conversation-derived; widen when other
sources ship. Item kind is encoded by class name (no ``owner_type``
field on the wire), so episode results never carry ambiguity.

SearchGroupProfile.title: SearchGroupProfile
SearchGroupProfile.description: The visible current group-profile items of a group scope, by kind.

SearchImageItem.title: SearchImageItem
SearchImageItem.description:
Image-memory hit — one appearance of one picture.

``id`` and ``image_id`` are different identities on purpose: ``id`` names
this *record* (a time, a provenance, a description), while ``image_id``
names the *file*, which is stored once however many records refer to it and
is what ``forget`` takes.

The three paths are memory-root-relative; a caller resolves them against
its own root. ``model_path`` is the copy to hand an answering model: the
``[images] model_edge`` copy (1024 px on the long side by default), the
same size the extraction model read the picture at.
``GET /memory/images/{image_id}?variant=model`` serves the same bytes by
id. ``original_path`` is the picture byte for byte as it arrived, for a
caller that wants it (a download, an export); it can be many times the
copy's size and visual tokens. ``thumbnail_path`` is the decider's copy,
small so it can look at many pictures cheaply; it is not meant for an
answer.

``name`` is the file name the client sent with this occurrence, when it
sent one. It is not an identity (the same picture may arrive under two
names) but it is the only handle a caller has for saying which picture of
its own input this memory is about.

SearchMethod.title: SearchMethod
SearchMethod.description:
The search method. Multi-round retrieval is the only one.

The keyword, vector, hybrid and agentic methods were removed with the
atomic facts the vector and hybrid routes ranked: a request naming one is
refused (see :data:`MULTIROUND_ONLY`).

SearchProfileItem.title: SearchProfileItem
SearchProfileItem.description:
A profile attached with ``include_profile``.

On a user scope, the owner's profile (at most one). On a group scope, the
member-in-group profiles of the asker and of the members the query names
(``owner_type = group``, ``group_id``, ``member_id``), holding only the
items the asker's windows allow -- never a personal profile. A user scope
with ``include_groups`` returns the owner's profile (``owner_type =
user``) and the owner's own profile in each group searched, cut the same
way; never another member's.

``score`` is ``None`` for direct fetches (``include_profile=true``
on its own does no ranking); a future query-aware lookup may fill
it in.

images.title: Images
images.description: Pictures that are part of the question. They are shown to a multi-round decider on every round; they create no memory and no reference.

SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest
SearchRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v2/memory/search``.

Callers name the memory owner with ``user_id`` or a group scope
(``group_id`` / ``group_ids`` / ``project_scope``) -- exactly one.
Internally the manager + compile_filters keep using ``owner_id`` /
``owner_type`` (the storage tables' columns); those are exposed as
derived properties so the rename only affects the wire contract, not the
internal recall plumbing.

An ``agent_id`` is refused with :data:`NO_AGENT_MEMORY`: EverOS 2.0 has no
agent memory.

SearchScope.title: SearchScope
SearchScope.description:
The scope a group search was answered in (docs/group-memory.md, 5.3).

A user search with ``include_groups`` returns one too: ``owner_type``
``user``, the user as the asker, and the groups searched alongside the
personal memory with the user's windows in each (``group_ids`` empty when
the user belongs to none).

SearchSource.title: SearchSource
SearchSource.description:
Where a group record comes from: its segment and the span it covers.

``from`` and ``to`` are epoch ms of the segment's first and last message
(a scene's: of its first member's first and its newest member's last);
``memcell_id`` is the segment, ``None`` for a scene, which has several.

SearchWindow.title: SearchWindow
SearchWindow.description: One of the asker's membership windows in one group, ``[from, to)`` ms.

SessionTarget.title: SessionTarget
SessionTarget.description: Every message of one of the group's sessions (owners and admins).

SupersededStatement.title: SupersededStatement
SupersededStatement.description: An earlier version a current constraint replaced.

TaskItem.title: TaskItem
TaskItem.description:
``GET /tasks/{task_id}`` -- one accepted request, in the Cloud's shape.

``id`` is the request id of the accepting call. Cloud also emits
``pending`` (accepted, boundary not run yet); this build never does, so a
client written for Cloud sees a subset of the statuses it already handles.

TriggerResponse.title: TriggerResponse
TriggerResponse.description:
Response body for ``POST /api/v2/ome/trigger``.

``status`` distinguishes three outcomes that were previously masked as
a single ``ok``:

- ``ok``: at least one strategy was dispatched and all runs settled
  within ``timeout``. Individual run outcomes are in ``runs`` (a
  ``dead_letter`` there is still ``ok`` at this level — the strategy
  *ran*, it just failed permanently).
- ``timeout``: at least one strategy was dispatched but the engine did
  not go idle within ``timeout``. Runs may be partially complete;
  poll ``GET /health`` for cascade convergence separately.
- ``not_dispatched``: no strategy was dispatched — the subscriber was
  rejected by one of the dispatch gates (``_routes_to`` / ``enabled`` /
  ``applies_to`` / ``Counter``). Common cause: forgetting
  ``force=true`` on a strategy that is ``enabled=false`` in ome.toml.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Not taken here: a body that names a group is a group forget (group_id, asker_id, target).

UndoForgetRequest.title: UndoForgetRequest
UndoForgetRequest.description:
Which picture's newest forget to undo, for which user.

Same fields as :class:`ForgetImageRequest` on purpose: an undo addresses
exactly what the forget addressed, and a caller that kept its forget
request can reuse it. The forget it reverses is the newest one for that
picture by that user that no earlier undo already reversed.

UndoForgetResponseData.title: UndoForgetResponseData
UndoForgetResponseData.description:
What an undo put back.

``applied`` is ``False`` when there was nothing to undo — the picture was
never forgotten, or an earlier undo already reversed it. The rest of the
payload is still filled in, so a caller sees the state it ends in rather
than having to ask again.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Refused (422): a conversation of a group is forgotten with POST /memory/forget and a session target.

UndoForgetSessionRequest.title: UndoForgetSessionRequest
UndoForgetSessionRequest.description: Which conversation's newest forget to undo, for which user.

UndoForgetSessionResponseData.title: UndoForgetSessionResponseData
UndoForgetSessionResponseData.description: What undoing a conversation's forget put back (``profiles``: items).

UnprocessedMessageDTO.title: UnprocessedMessageDTO
UnprocessedMessageDTO.description:
A raw message still in the boundary-detection buffer.

No extracted memcell yet, no owner inference yet (attribution
happens at boundary detection). Returned by ``/search`` **only when**
``filters.session_id`` is present as a top-level eq predicate —
unprocessed messages have no ``user_id`` to filter on, so session is
the only meaningful query dimension.

asker_id.title: Asker Id
asker_id.description: Who asks; required for a group unless the identity header names them. Recorded on the new version as edited_by.

expected_version.title: Expected Version
expected_version.description: The version the caller read; default: id.

UpdateMemoryRequest.title: UpdateMemoryRequest
UpdateMemoryRequest.description:
A person's change of one memory: a new version, linked to the old one.

Fields a kind takes: an episode or a scene ``subject``, ``summary`` and
``content``; a picture memory ``description`` and ``ocr``; a profile item
``description``. A field left out keeps the stored text. ``hold`` (default
true) keeps the new version from the model's later updates; ``hold:
false`` alone releases a held version. ``expected_version`` (default:
``id``) is the version the caller read; when a newer one exists the
answer is 409 and nothing is written.

UpdateMemoryResponseData.title: UpdateMemoryResponseData
UpdateMemoryResponseData.description: The version a change wrote (or the current one, when nothing changed).

UserConditionTarget.title: UserConditionTarget
UserConditionTarget.description:
The memories of some kinds whose time falls in ``[start, end)``.

Epoch ms; either bound may be left open. A memory's time is when what it
says happened; a profile item's, when it was last observed.

UserForgetRequest.title: UserForgetRequest
UserForgetRequest.description:
A forget in one user's memory, by target; a dry run unless told not to.

``dry_run`` (default **true**) changes nothing and answers with what the
real run would touch; send ``dry_run: false`` to forget. A real forget
answers with its ``forget_id``, the token ``/memory/forget/undo`` takes.

UserForgetResponseData.title: UserForgetResponseData
UserForgetResponseData.description:
What a forget in a user's memory touched (or would, on a dry run).

Records are named as a read names them (``<user>_<entry>``), profile items
by ``item_id``. ``episodes`` and ``scenes`` are the versions taken out of
default reads -- marked forgotten, or (a picture's forget) replaced by the
``new_episodes`` / ``new_scenes`` written without the picture. ``images``
are picture files taken out of circulation.

UserImageTarget.title: UserImageTarget
UserImageTarget.description: One picture by content hash: its memories, and the references to it.

UserMessageTarget.title: UserMessageTarget
UserMessageTarget.description:
Messages of one of the user's conversations, by id: each segment that
held one is remembered again without it.

UserOwnerTarget.title: UserOwnerTarget
UserOwnerTarget.description: Everything of the user: episodes, pictures, scenes, the whole profile.

UserRecordTarget.title: UserRecordTarget
UserRecordTarget.description:
Records by id, of any kind: episodes, picture memories, scenes,
profile items (and replaced values, by the id a read lists).

UserSessionTarget.title: UserSessionTarget
UserSessionTarget.description: Everything one conversation established for the user.

UserUndoForgetRequest.title: UserUndoForgetRequest
UserUndoForgetRequest.description: Undo one forget of a user by its id (the ``forget_id`` it answered).

UserUndoForgetResponseData.title: UserUndoForgetResponseData
UserUndoForgetResponseData.description:
What an undo of a user's forget put back; ``applied: false`` when it was
undone already. ``profile_items`` counts items.
